command:
set -eu
cleanup() {
  firewall-cmd --zone=public --remove-interface=vethfw0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  ip netns del fwtest >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  kill "$(cat /tmp/fw8080.pid)" "$(cat /tmp/fw8081.pid)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f /tmp/fw8080.pid /tmp/fw8081.pid /tmp/fw8080.log /tmp/fw8081.log
}
trap cleanup EXIT
python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 0.0.0.0 >/tmp/fw8080.log 2>&1 & echo $! >/tmp/fw8080.pid
python3 -m http.server 8081 --bind 0.0.0.0 >/tmp/fw8081.log 2>&1 & echo $! >/tmp/fw8081.pid
ip netns add fwtest
ip link add vethfw0 type veth peer name vethfw1
ip link set vethfw1 netns fwtest
ip addr add 192.0.2.1/30 dev vethfw0
ip link set vethfw0 up
ip netns exec fwtest ip addr add 192.0.2.2/30 dev vethfw1
ip netns exec fwtest ip link set lo up
ip netns exec fwtest ip link set vethfw1 up
firewall-cmd --zone=public --add-interface=vethfw0 >/dev/null
sleep 1
printf '%s\n' '--- both destination ports are listening ---'
ss -lntp '( sport = :8080 or sport = :8081 )'
printf '%s\n' '--- allowed TCP/8080 through public-zone ingress ---'
ip netns exec fwtest curl --noproxy '*' --connect-timeout 3 -sS -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP status %{http_code}\n' http://192.0.2.1:8080/
printf '%s\n' '--- unrelated TCP/8081 through same ingress (must reject) ---'
set +e
blocked_output=$(ip netns exec fwtest curl --noproxy '*' --connect-timeout 3 -sS http://192.0.2.1:8081/ 2>&1)
blocked_rc=$?
set -e
printf 'curl exit=%s\n%s\n' "$blocked_rc" "$blocked_output"
[ "$blocked_rc" -ne 0 ]
